```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Djebli_2017_FV60165_rabbit"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Djebli_2017_FV60165_rabbit"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s13318-016-0319-4> (open access)

FV-60165 is a src tyrosine kinase inhibitor developed for corneal
neovascularisation. It was given as its lipophilic prodrug FV-80228, which is
hydrolysed to FV-60165 in the tear film and corneal epithelium; prodrug
concentrations were almost all below the limit of quantification, so only
FV-60165 was modelled. The model describes FV-60165 in four matrices of the
anterior segment of the rabbit eye: tear fluid, naso-lacrimal duct, cornea and
aqueous humor.

# Population

Forty-two male HY79b pigmented rabbits (approximately 2-2.5 kg) received two
30 uL drops of a 0.6% prodrug formulation into both eyes, 10 minutes apart
(180 ug per drop, 360 ug per eye). Twenty-one rabbits received a solution in
7% 2-hydroxypropyl-beta-cyclodextrin (pH 5) and 21 a nanosuspension in 0.5%
carboxymethylcellulose with 0.015% Tween 80 (pH 7.4). Sampling was destructive:
three rabbits per formulation were killed at each of 0.083, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4
and 8 h, and tear fluid, naso-lacrimal duct, cornea and aqueous humor were
collected from both eyes. Each eye was analysed as a separate individual, giving
84 individuals and 336 FV-60165 concentrations (Djebli 2017 Sections 2.2, 2.3
and 3).

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Djebli_2017_FV60165_rabbit")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries a source comment in
`inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Djebli_2017_FV60165_rabbit.R`. The table collects
them.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| Structure: tear -> naso-lacrimal duct (k12), tear -> cornea (k13), cornea <-> aqueous humor (Q), loss from duct (Clnl), aqueous humor (Clah) and cornea (Clc) | -- | Figure 1; Table 1 footnotes |
| `lfdepot` (F1) | 0.300 | Table 1 |
| `lk_tear_nasolacrimal_duct_soln` (k12, solution) | 0.299 1/h | Table 1 |
| `lk_tear_nasolacrimal_duct_nanosusp` (k12, nanosuspension) | 0.259 1/h | Table 1 |
| `k12 = theta_i * FORMULATION + theta_j * (1 - FORMULATION)` | -- | Section 3 (Results) |
| `lk_tear_cornea` (k13) | 0.340 1/h | Table 1 |
| `lq_cornea_aqueous_humour` (Q) | 0.136 uL/h | Table 1 |
| `lcl_nasolacrimal_duct` (Clnl) | 275 uL/h | Table 1 |
| `lcl_aqueous_humour` (Clah) | 231 uL/h | Table 1 |
| `f_cl_cornea` (Clc = 0.1 * Clah, fixed) | 0.1 | Section 3 (Results); Figure 1 legend |
| `lv_tear` (V1) | 155 uL | Table 1 |
| `lv_nasolacrimal_duct` (V2) | 1.24 uL | Table 1 |
| `lv_cornea` (V3) | 42.8 uL | Table 1 |
| `lv_aqueous_humour` (V4) | 218 uL | Table 1 |
| IIV (CV%): F1 60.5, k12 80.0, k13 45.3, Q 172, Clnl 90.5, Clah 92.0, V1 153, V2 437, V3 51.1, V4 265 | log-normal variance = log((CV/100)^2 + 1) | Table 1; Section 3 |
| `propSd_*` (one sigma, all matrices) | 0.491% | Table 1; Section 3 |
| Dose entering the tears: one third of each drop (60 ug) | -- | Section 2.5.2; confirmed against Figure 6 below |

# Model

```{r load-model}
mod <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Djebli_2017_FV60165_rabbit"))
mod_typical <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
```

All doses go into the `tear` state. Observation rows use the ODE state name
and `dvid = 1`; rxode2 returns all four concentrations as columns on every
observation row.

```{r dosing-helper}
# Two drops 10 min apart. Section 2.5.2: a maximum of 10 uL of each 30 uL
# drop stays in the tear film, and one third of the instilled dose was
# entered into the analysis dataset, so each drop contributes 60 ug.
dose_per_drop <- 180 / 3
drop_times <- c(0, 10 / 60)

make_events <- function(ids, form, obs_times) {
  doses <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = drop_times) |>
    mutate(amt = dose_per_drop, evid = 1L, cmt = "tear", dvid = NA_integer_)
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "tear", dvid = 1L)
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
    mutate(FORM_FV60165_NANOSUSP = form)
}

formulation_label <- c("0" = "Solution", "1" = "Nanosuspension")
matrix_label <- c(
  Ctear = "Tears",
  Cnasolacrimal_duct = "Nasolacrimal duct",
  Ccornea = "Cornea",
  Caqueous_humour = "Aqueous humor"
)
```

# Typical-value profiles (Figure 6)

```{r typical}
typ_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 16, by = 0.05), drop_times)))
ev_typ <- bind_rows(
  make_events(1L, 0L, typ_times),
  make_events(2L, 1L, typ_times)
)
sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_typical,
  ev_typ,
  keep = "FORM_FV60165_NANOSUSP",
  returnType = "data.frame"
)
typ_long <- sim_typ |>
  select(id, time, FORM_FV60165_NANOSUSP, all_of(names(matrix_label))) |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(names(matrix_label)), names_to = "matrix", values_to = "conc") |>
  mutate(
    Formulation = formulation_label[as.character(FORM_FV60165_NANOSUSP)],
    Matrix = factor(matrix_label[matrix], levels = matrix_label)
  )
```

```{r figure-6, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5}
ggplot(
  filter(typ_long, time > 0, time <= 12.2),
  aes(time, conc, colour = Formulation, linetype = Matrix)
) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(1e-3, 1e3)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Nanosuspension = "red", Solution = "blue")) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)",
    y = "Tissue concentration (ng/uL)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 6 of Djebli 2017 (typical rabbit eye)."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

## Comparison against Figure 6

Figure 6 of the paper is a raster image. The maintainers digitised it at seven
times between 2 and 12 h (after the curves for the four matrices have
separated), for both formulations. The axis calibration used the printed tick
marks; the reading error is a few percent.

```{r figure-6-digitised}
fig6 <- tibble::tribble(

# Solve the typical eye at the digitised times under two dosing readings:
# the protocol (two 60 ug drops 10 min apart) and a single 120 ug bolus.
predict_fig6 <- function(dose_rows) {
  out <- lapply(0:1, function(f) {
    ev <- bind_rows(
      mutate(dose_rows, id = 1L, evid = 1L, cmt = "tear", dvid = NA_integer_),
      tibble::tibble(id = 1L, time = unique(fig6$time), amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "tear", dvid = 1L)
    ) |>
      arrange(time, desc(evid)) |>
      mutate(FORM_FV60165_NANOSUSP = f)
    rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typical, ev, returnType = "data.frame") |>
      select(time, all_of(names(matrix_label))) |>
      pivot_longer(-time, names_to = "matrix", values_to = "pred") |>
      mutate(form = f)
  })
  inner_join(fig6, bind_rows(out), by = c("time", "form", "matrix")) |>
    mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (pred - conc) / conc)
}

chk_split <- predict_fig6(tibble::tibble(time = drop_times, amt = dose_per_drop))
chk_single <- predict_fig6(tibble::tibble(time = 0, amt = 2 * dose_per_drop))

chk_split |>
  mutate(
    Formulation = formulation_label[as.character(form)],
    Matrix = matrix_label[matrix]
  ) |>
  group_by(Formulation, Matrix) |>
  summarise(
    median_pct = round(median(pct_diff), 1),
    max_abs_pct = round(max(abs(pct_diff)), 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  rename(
    "Median % difference" = median_pct,
    "Max |% difference|" = max_abs_pct
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Packaged model (typical eye, two 60 ug drops) versus digitised Figure 6, 2-12 h.")

bind_rows(
  mutate(chk_split, dosing = "Two 60 ug drops, 10 min apart"),
  mutate(chk_single, dosing = "Single 120 ug bolus")
) |>
  group_by(dosing) |>
  summarise(
    median_pct = round(median(pct_diff), 2),
    p90_abs_pct = round(unname(quantile(abs(pct_diff), 0.9)), 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  rename(
    "Dosing reading" = dosing,
    "Median % difference" = median_pct,
    "90th percentile |% difference|" = p90_abs_pct
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "The protocol dosing reproduces Figure 6; a single bolus of the same total is biased low.")

stopifnot(
  # A mis-transcribed rate, volume, F1 or dose moves every matrix by tens of
  # percent; digitisation error is a few percent.
  abs(median(chk_split$pct_diff)) < 2,
  quantile(abs(chk_split$pct_diff), 0.9) < 6,
  # The protocol dosing fits the figure better than one bolus of the same total.
  median(abs(chk_split$pct_diff)) < median(abs(chk_single$pct_diff))
)
```

## Closed-form check of the tear compartment

The tear compartment receives only the bolus doses and loses drug by two
first-order routes, so its concentration has a closed form,
`C(t) = 1000 * F1 * sum(D * exp(-(k12 + k13) * (t - t_dose))) / V1`. Both sides
use the same parameters, so the difference is pure ODE-solver error.

```{r tear-closed-form}
tear_cf <- typ_long |>
  filter(matrix == "Ctear", time > 0) |>
  mutate(
    k12 = ifelse(FORM_FV60165_NANOSUSP == 1, 0.259, 0.299),
    cf = 1000 * 0.300 * dose_per_drop / 155 *
      (exp(-(k12 + 0.340) * time) +
        ifelse(time >= drop_times[2], exp(-(k12 + 0.340) * (time - drop_times[2])), 0)),
    rel_err = abs(conc - cf) / cf
  )
max(tear_cf$rel_err)
stopifnot(max(tear_cf$rel_err) < 1e-4)
```

# Virtual cohort and stochastic simulation

A cohort of 100 eyes per formulation is simulated with the paper's inter-
individual variability. The paper fitted every eye as one individual; eyes of
the same rabbit are treated as independent here, as in the paper.

```{r stochastic}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20170128)
n_per_arm <- 100L
sto_times <- sort(unique(c(0, 0.083, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, seq(0, 12, by = 0.25))))
ev_sto <- bind_rows(
  make_events(seq_len(n_per_arm), 0L, sto_times),
  make_events(n_per_arm + seq_len(n_per_arm), 1L, sto_times)
)
sim_sto <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  ev_sto,
  keep = "FORM_FV60165_NANOSUSP",
  returnType = "data.frame"
)
sto_long <- sim_sto |>
  select(id, time, FORM_FV60165_NANOSUSP, all_of(names(matrix_label))) |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(names(matrix_label)), names_to = "matrix", values_to = "conc") |>
  mutate(
    Formulation = formulation_label[as.character(FORM_FV60165_NANOSUSP)],
    Matrix = factor(matrix_label[matrix], levels = matrix_label)
  )
```

```{r vpc, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5}
sto_long |>
  filter(time > 0) |>
  group_by(Matrix, time) |>
  summarise(
    p05 = quantile(conc, 0.05),
    p50 = median(conc),
    p95 = quantile(conc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, p50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~Matrix, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)",
    y = "Concentration (ng/uL)",
    caption = paste(
      "Median and 5th-95th percentiles, both formulations pooled.",
      "Compare with the prediction intervals of Figure 4 of Djebli 2017."
    )
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

The observed concentrations spanned 0.0202 to 6260 ng/uL across the four
matrices (Section 3); the simulated 5th-95th percentile bands cover the same
orders of magnitude, with aqueous humor lowest and tears highest at early
times, as in Figure 4.

# PKNCA

Non-compartmental parameters over 0-12 h are computed for each formulation in
the cornea (the target tissue) and the tears. The paper reports no NCA values,
so the table is descriptive.

```{r pknca}
nca_conc <- sto_long |>
  filter(matrix %in% c("Ccornea", "Ctear"), !is.na(conc)) |>
  mutate(treatment = paste(Formulation, Matrix, sep = " / ")) |>
  select(id, time, conc, treatment)

nca_dose <- nca_conc |>
  distinct(id, treatment) |>
  tidyr::expand_grid(time = drop_times) |>
  mutate(amt = dose_per_drop)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, conc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_dose, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0,
  end = 12,
  cmax = TRUE,
  tmax = TRUE,
  auclast = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "auclast")) |>
  group_by(treatment, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(median = signif(median(PPORRES), 3), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median) |>
  rename(
    "Formulation / matrix" = treatment,
    "Cmax (ng/uL)" = cmax,
    "Tmax (h)" = tmax,
    "AUC0-12 (h*ng/uL)" = auclast
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Median PKNCA parameters, 100 simulated eyes per formulation.")
```

The typical-value cornea profile peaks at about 1.8 h, at 178 ng/uL for the
solution and 184 ng/uL for the nanosuspension (Figure 6); the nanosuspension's slower
loss to the naso-lacrimal duct (k12 0.259 versus 0.299 1/h) leaves slightly
more drug in the tears and cornea at late times.

```{r cornea-peak}
cornea_peak <- typ_long |>
  filter(matrix == "Ccornea") |>
  group_by(Formulation) |>
  slice_max(conc, n = 1) |>
  ungroup()
cornea_peak |> select(Formulation, time, conc)
stopifnot(
  all(abs(cornea_peak$time - 1.8) <= 0.1),
  abs(cornea_peak$conc[cornea_peak$Formulation == "Solution"] - 178) < 1,
  abs(cornea_peak$conc[cornea_peak$Formulation == "Nanosuspension"] - 184) < 1
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Dose entering the model.** Section 2.5.2 states that one third of the
  instilled dose was entered into the analysis dataset, because at most 10 uL
  of each 30 uL drop stays in the tear film. The model is dosed with 60 ug of
  prodrug FV-80228 per drop, at 0 and 10 min. Dose amounts are prodrug mass, not
  FV-60165 molar equivalents (MW 554 vs 450): the comparison with Figure 6
  above reproduces the published typical profiles with this reading, whereas a
  molar conversion would put every curve about 19% low. The relative
  bioavailability F1 absorbs both the prodrug-to-drug conversion and the loss
  from the eye surface.
* **Form of the inter-individual variability.** The paper selected a
  "proportional error model" for IIV, `P = TV * (1 + eta)`, and Table 1 prints
  `100 * omega` as a CV%: the 95% confidence intervals printed for each CV are
  reproduced as `CV * sqrt(1 +/- 1.96 * RSE)` with the RSE on the variance,
  which fixes that scale. The proportional form cannot be simulated with these
  values: with a CV of 437% on V2, `1 + eta` is negative, and so is the
  naso-lacrimal duct volume, in about 41% of eyes. The packaged model therefore
  uses log-normal IIV at the same CV, `omega^2 = log((CV/100)^2 + 1)` (for
  example 3.00 for V2 and 0.312 for F1). The typical-value profiles are
  unaffected; the spread of the stochastic cohort below is the log-normal one,
  not the paper's. The paper reports high eta shrinkage on several of these
  parameters (for example 91.5% on k12 and 98.5% on V3), so the IIV is weakly
  informed by the data in either form.
* **Residual error.** The paper estimated one proportional sigma (0.491%) for
  all four matrices. nlmixr2 needs a separate residual parameter per endpoint,
  so the same value is carried four times (`propSd_Ctear`,
  `propSd_Cnasolacrimal_duct`, `propSd_Ccornea`, `propSd_Caqueous_humour`). A refit that
  wants the paper's constraint must tie them.
* **Formulation coding.** The paper does not say which formulation it coded as
  1. The two estimated k12 values are carried as separate parameters and
  `FORM_FV60165_NANOSUSP` (1 = nanosuspension) only selects between them, so
  the choice of coding does not change any prediction. The IIV on k12 is shared
  by both formulations.
* **Compartment names.** The four states use the library's bare ocular-anatomy
  compartment names `tear`, `nasolacrimal_duct`, `cornea` and `aqueous_humour`,
  registered with this model alongside the existing `retina` and `vitreous`.
  The tear compartment's matrix is recorded as tear fluid (collected on
  Schirmer strips); the duct and cornea were assayed as tissue homogenates.
* **Bioavailability parameter.** F1 is carried as `lfdepot`, the library's
  usual name for the bioavailability of the dosed compartment, and applied to
  `tear` (the dose site) rather than to a `depot` state.
* **Contralateral eyes.** Both eyes of each rabbit were fitted as separate
  individuals with no shared random effect, and are simulated that way here.
